direction.broader_thesis: Agent orchestration is an underexplored design space. Most systems make orchestration choices implicitly — hard-coded, never measured, never optimized. Making them explicit, measurable, and optimizable is the research contribution.
direction.paper_1_thesis: Internal language choice should be studied as an orchestration policy over explicit agent messages — not as a claim about hidden cognition.
direction.generalized_formulation: For any orchestration variable σ: π(m_t, x_t) → σ_t. Language is σ = ℓ. But σ can be memory policy, planning depth, retry strategy, verification cadence, context allocation, observation granularity, tool scheduling, delegation topology, instruction hierarchy, or reasoning format.
direction.optimization_target: max_π U(π) = Success − λ_c·Cost − λ_t·Latency − λ_s·SafetyRisk (applies to ALL orchestration variables, not just language)
direction.key_insight: Language is Paper 1 because it's the most tractable (easy to manipulate, easy to measure, clear priors). But the harness generalizes to any orchestration variable.
direction.danqi_caveat: World is changing fast — revisit settings, models, benchmarks before fall. Infrastructure and harness should be model-agnostic.

interaction_hypotheses: Language × memory: shorter language = more memory budget (multiplicative)
Language × planning: planning text is highest compression target
Reasoning format × verification: structured formats enable automatic verification
Memory × observation: summarized observations are easier to retain
Planning × retry: better plans → fewer retries → lower total cost
Context allocation × everything: meta-variable that mediates all others
